contract.schema: Six non-null I64 columns: id, customer, symbol, day, qty, price
contract.consistency: Read-your-writes in one process; DuckDB native batches flush before acknowledgement
contract.durability: In-memory only. No process/power-loss durability or replication claim.
contract.atomicity: No cross-call transaction. Valid batches and adapter argument rejection are tested; general engine error/OOM atomicity remains unqualified.
contract.idempotency: None: IDs are unique by construction, not enforced by a primary-key constraint
contract.retry: No mutation retries; any unexpected error fails the case
contract.query_path: Parsed SQL INSERT VALUES versus quoted-target Rayfall insert, including source parsing
contract.typed_path: DuckDB C Appender + per-batch flush versus Rayforce C typed vectors/table + fixed Rayfall dispatch
contract.append_payload: id=x, customer=x%10000, symbol=x%256, day=x%30, qty=1+x%100, price=100+x%9901
contract.read_and_cache_scope: Fresh in-memory processes load the same CSV; reads are hot/recent, not OS-cold
contract.oracle: Every old and new row is exported in ID order and matched to independently generated canonical CSV bytes by length and SHA256
contract.timing: Actual first-write-start to last-write-finish includes intervening dispatch/logging and the middle read for multi-request cells. Setup, initial/final read and export are separately timed.
contract.limits: Single writer; no distributed or availability claim. Both engines use the same CPU/memory cap. Native adapter batches contain 1..10000 rows. CSV witness exports are verification artifacts, not engine persistence.

writes.scope: Measured first call start to last call finish, including intervening plan handling/logging and the middle probe when multiple requests exist. Import, initial/final read and export are separate. Request percentiles with one/few batches do not establish tails.

native.cpu_utilization_scope: Cgroup CPU includes runtime, wrapper and accounting commands; denominator is Docker StartedAt to FinishedAt, parsed at microsecond resolution. CPU snapshot precedes the final accounting commands/exit, so their final CPU is not included. Driver uptime window has 10 ms resolution; per-query CPU and wall time are separate exact-clock samples.

block_io.scope: Whole-container kernel block-I/O accounting, including wrapper. Empty counters/cached reads do not establish zero physical host I/O; Docker Desktop file sharing can perform work outside this cgroup. Not logical engine bytes, device latency or queue depth.

sampled_resources.scope: Approximately 100 ms plus API/inspection overhead; arithmetic sample mean, not heap or time-weighted mean. Sampling can miss short peaks; use native cgroup memory.peak and process RSS too. Docker daemon/VM overhead excluded.

block_io.scope: Whole-container kernel block-I/O accounting, including wrapper. Empty counters/cached reads do not establish zero physical host I/O; Docker Desktop file sharing can perform work outside this cgroup. Not logical engine bytes, device latency or queue depth.

sampled_resources.scope: Approximately 100 ms plus API/inspection overhead; arithmetic sample mean, not heap or time-weighted mean. Sampling can miss short peaks; use native cgroup memory.peak and process RSS too. Docker daemon/VM overhead excluded.
